chunks: Aṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn ruled concerning a man who died and bequeathed all of his wealth, or most of it, saying: “The bequest is to be returned to what is proper, and the inheritance of the inheritors is to be left for them.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمِيرَاثِ: the rightful heirs entitled to inherit
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفِ: what is proper, recognized, and legally acceptable in context
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةَ: a bequest or testamentary disposition made by the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone bequeaths all or most of his wealth before death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on excessive bequests made at death. It states that a will must be limited to what is recognized as proper, while the fixed inheritance rights of the heirs must remain محفوظ and not be overridden.
